Roosters: 1. James Tedesco 2. Daniel Tupou 3. Billy Smith 4. Robert Toia 5. Mark Nawaqanitawase 6. Daly Cherry-Evans 7. Sam Walker 8. Naufahu Whyte 9. Reece Robson 10. Lindsay Collins 11. Salesi Foketi 12. Siua Wong 13. Victor Radley Bench:14. Connor Watson 15. Angus Crichton 16. Nat Butcher 17. Spencer Leniu 18. Hugo Savala 19. Cody Ramsey Reserves: 20. Egan Butcher 21. Tommy Talau 22. Benaiah Ioelu

Officials

Referee: Adam Gee Touchies: Phil Henderson, Tyson Brough

Bunker: Ashley Klein

Prediction: The Dolphins were very impressive two weeks ago against the Warriors, restricting them to one try, before unleashing their signature attacking blitz after the break. Previously this season they have allowed teams to get away to big head starts before mounting their fightback, a ploy which just won't stand up in the finals. They appear to have taken note and their defensive work in New Zealand was outstanding. They will need to be at their very best once more against the Roosters, who have the attacking flair to cause them plenty of problems.

The Roosters were simply too good for the Sharks last week, after going very close to beating the Panthers the week before. They have plenty of experience across the park, with Daly Cherry-Evans putting in a much better performance against the Sharks in combination with the hard running Hugo Savala. Outside those two, the Roosters backline bristles with attacking weapons, with Robert Toia and Mark Nawaqanitawase in unstoppable form, James Tedesco always lurking, and Sam Walker returning at halfback.

But, as we all know, the backs don't win the big games, they just determine the score, and the Roosters have a pack that is the match of any in the league. Naufahu Whyte, Lindsay Collins and Siua Wong were at their destructive best against the Sharks. Add the menace of Victor Radley and Spencer Leniu, plus the returning Angus Crichton, and there isn't a weakness across the middle or on the edges.

The Dolphins will have to match the Roosters forwards, with Thomas Flegler, Tom Gilbert, Max Plath, Kulikefu Finefeuiaki, Ray Stone and Francis Molo all in for a big night. If they can negate the Roosters pack, we all know how devastating the Dolphins halves and backs can be.

On paper this is very difficult to pick. It is one of those games that might come down to a key error, a moment of madness, the luck of the bounce or the whims of the referee's six again calls. Whoever wins, we are sure to be treated to an entertaining clash.

Tip: Dolphins by 10

PointsBet odds: Dolphins $1.74 (-2.5 $2) Roosters $2.10 (+2.5 $1.83)

Sunday, September 27
Penrith Panthers vs. Newcastle Knights
Accor Stadium, 4pm (AEST)
Panthers: 1. Dylan Edwards 2. Thomas Jenkins 3. Blaize Talagi 4. Casey McLean 5. Brian To'o 6. Jack Cole 7. Nathan Cleary 8. Moses Leota 9. Mitch Kenny 10. Lindsay Smith 11. Isaiah Papali'i 12. Liam Martin 13. Isaah Yeo Bench: 14. Jack Cogger 15. Scott Sorensen 16. Liam Henry 17. Billy Phillips 18. Luke Garner 19. Billy Scott Reserves: 20. Luron Patea 21. Freddy Lussick 22. Izack Tago

Knights: 1. Kalyn Ponga 2. Dominic Young 3. Dane Gagai 4. Bradman Best 5. Greg Marzhew 6. Fletcher Sharpe 7. Sandon Smith 8. Tyson Frizell 9. Phoenix Crossland 10. Cody Hopwood 11. Jermaine McEwen 12. Francis Manuleleua 13. Mathew Croker Bench: 14. Harrison Graham 15. Lachlan Crouch 16. Pasami Saulo 17. Dylan Lucas 18. Fletcher Hunt 19. Thomas Cant Reserves: 20. Kyle McCarthy 21. Elijah Leaumoana 22. Toby Winter

Officials

Referee: Gerard Sutton Touchies: Matt Noyen, Daniel Luttringer

Bunker: Chris Butler

Prediction: The best team of the 2026 season meets the hottest team of the 2026 finals in what should be another great game in front of a large crowd in Homebush.

The Panthers didn't have it all their way two weeks ago when defeating the Roosters, they were well-matched and needed a wobbly Nathan Cleary field goal to break a late deadlock. Cleary has been the focus ever since, as first he avoided suspension for a dangerous contact charge, and then set about rehabilitating an injured foot. The Panthers have proven they can win games without Cleary, but his coolness under pressure is invaluable in the biggest games.

The Knights are playing with the casino's money at this stage. After finishing last in 2025, making the finals surpassed anyone's expectations. To be playing in the Preliminary Final is an incredible achievement for coach Justin Holbrook and his team, especially considering they are without star half Dylan Brown. They simply have to keep playing the way they have been playing. Fast moving defence, free flowing ball movement from anywhere on the field, and total belief in their ability to beat anyone. Phoenix Crossland, Fletcher Sharpe, Kalyn Ponga, Bradman Best, Dan Gagai, Dom Young, the Knights have weapons across the field. Without Jacob Saifiti, they are a little light on up front, but veteran Tyson Frizell has stepped up in the middle and the Knights back-row ranks, strengthened now by the surprise return of Dylan Lucas, have been simply brilliant.

The big question is; can the Knights execute their attacking style against the best defence in the business? They played just the once this season, with the Panthers winning 44-12. We know how good the Panthers are. We have seen them dominate the big games for years. Cleary and Dylan Edwards orchestrating the attack, Isaah Yeo and Liam Martin leading the defence. The Panthers are the best team in the competition for good reason and they stand between the other three teams and the premiership title. I think they'll return to the big dance this year.

Tip: Panthers by 14

PointsBet odds: Panthers $1.26 (-10.5 $1.95) Knights $3.80 (+10.5 $1.87)

All odds correct at time of publication. Check pointsbet.com.au for the latest.

stories.headline: How San Diego Padres have become a flashpoint in MLB's labor battle
stories.summary: Is San Diego why baseball needs a salary cap -- or a shining example of why it doesn't? It depends who you ask.
stories.body:
ON THE DAY the San Diego Padres' new ownership group was introduced, Manny Machado did some quick math. When the team was sold in 2012, he noted, the purchase price was $800 million. Fourteen years later, the franchise had sold for $3.9 billion -- nearly five times the amount.

"In my business, I wish I could do that investment," said Machado, the Padres' star third baseman. "That's a great return."

At a time when Major League Baseball is attempting to upend its economic model by instituting a salary cap, the Padres have emerged as a beacon for players and union officials who believe a level playing field can exist without one.

In their minds, the Padres' late owner, Peter Seidler, provided the blueprint -- by pouring money into a small-market franchise, elevating the roster to championship contention, turning the ballpark into a destination spot and, after his death, netting a record sale price. Seidler might have absorbed losses along the way, but, in their minds, it was worth it. His peers, they believe, could and should follow.

To others, particularly those who pine for a cap-and-floor system in a new collective bargaining agreement, that rationale is incomplete.

They see the Padres as an outlier and a cautionary tale. Their sale price was inflated as a Southern California franchise in a one-sport town. Their trajectory -- spending so high that a loan was needed for liquidity, a generational talent in Juan Soto traded for the purpose of getting under the luxury tax threshold, a barren farm system and an unsustainable payroll -- is the plight of a team unable to hang with bigger spenders in an open market. Even if other franchises wanted to follow in the Padres' footsteps, they can't, league officials and rival owners argue because their situation is unique.

MLB and the MLB Players' Association are in the midst of a contentious labor fight, and the Padres have become a convenient symbol for both sides. Of inspiration or caution. Of business acumen or reckless spending. Of the possibilities under a free-market system or the pitfalls that come with one.

"You can say it's unique, you can say it's not," said Padres infielder Jake Cronenworth, a member of the MLBPA's executive subcommittee. "But every club has the ability to do what we did -- invest in a good product on the field, invest in the community, and see what happens."

TODAY'S PADRES WOULD be unrecognizable to the 2019 iteration. That team ranked 24th in payroll and ultimately missed the playoffs for a 13th consecutive year.

"No one wanted to play here," said Machado, who joined the team that spring. "We were in the bottom tier of organizations."

The following year, in November 2020, Seidler assumed full control of the Padres, taking over as chairman after his business partner, Ron Fowler, stepped down. Over the next three years, the payroll jumped from $180 million to $225 million to more than $250 million by 2023, trailing only the New York Yankees and New York Mets.

The Padres now set franchise attendance records on a near-annual basis, surpassing 3 million fans every year since 2023. In 2026, they notched their fifth consecutive winning season and should soon capture their third straight playoff berth. Both would be firsts in franchise history. And though the payroll dropped significantly the year after Seidler's death in November 2023, the Padres elevated back into the top 10 in 2025 and 2026.

"When you invest in your team, you invest in your organization, not only do you get good players to come and want to play and put yourself in good situations to go win a championship," Machado said, "but you also get a lot of fans to come out here and support."

The Padres, who were one of the largest recipients of revenue sharing in the early 2010s, have paid into revenue sharing every year since 2023, an indication of their massive growth under Seidler. They did so despite ranking 24th in market size, as outlined by the current CBA. As Machado sees it, the Padres' success -- in a significantly limited market, with Mexico to the South, the Pacific Ocean to the West, the desert to the East and the Dodgers to the North -- means others can also do it.

"But you got to want it," Machado said. "And ownership wanted it here."

The Padres' new owners, José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones, have expressed a similar level of desire. Their plans, though, remain vague, at least in part because there's no telling what MLB's economic model will look like beyond this season.

At the least, their local media revenue should receive a boost. In May 2023, the Padres became the first team to lose their regional sports network, a product of the Diamond Sports Group bankruptcy proceedings that prompted the cancellation of a 20-year, $1.2 billion local media deal. They've been in a sort of limbo since.

MLB will sell all of its national rights and most, if not all, of its local rights after the 2028 season, a development that is widely expected to bring a major influx of cash. In the leadup to that, both the league and the union have made proposals that would prompt more sharing of local media revenue than under the current system.

"If that does happen," Padres CEO Erik Greupner said, "I think no team stands to benefit more than the Padres."

MLB has touted the equal distribution of local media as part of its cap-and-floor proposal, while the MLBPA has pitched a change in revenue sharing that would prompt teams to share more of their local media while keeping more of their stadium revenue. It's an idea that is in many ways inspired by what Seidler accomplished.

As Bruce Meyer, MLBPA interim executive director, said in June: "We want to encourage more San Diegos."

Union leaders don't view Seidler as a man who spent recklessly in hopes of winning a championship before his death, with little care for the future. They see an owner who operated his franchise like a shrewd businessman and knew the best way to make money was to invest in his product. Greupner, Seidler's right-hand man for the entirety of his ownership, said Seidler viewed the Padres through decade-long increments. Spending lavishly on players was merely "the first step" toward building revenues high enough to support bigger payrolls.

To Cronenworth, an oft-referenced Seidler quote speaks perfectly to that: There's a risk to doing nothing.

"And it's true," Cronenworth said. "It's true in investments, it's true in our own personal lives. It's true in everything. But if you don't take that risk, you never know what's on the other side."

IN THE MINDS of baseball's owners, the success of a team in Southern California is too unique -- the location too coveted -- to copy.

The Padres' sale price trumped the previous record for a baseball franchise set in 2020, when Steve Cohen purchased the Mets for $2.4 billion. Just eight days after Feliciano and Jones were introduced on Aug. 24, longtime Los Angeles Angels owner Arte Moreno reached a handshake deal to sell his team to Stan Kroenke for $4 billion.

According to Forbes, the Padres' operating income -- a measure of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization -- was a combined negative-$270 million from 2021 to 2024 before jumping to plus-$32 million in 2025. It will finish nearly flat, according to Forbes' projection, in 2026. That they sold for a record amount in spite of that, not to mention a reported $300 million in debt, is notable.

And then the Angels, who were essentially run into the ground for the past decade, topped that price, a shock to many in the industry. But people in league circles were quick to note that the valuation of MLB franchises continues to lag behind that of the NBA and the NFL: The NBA's Portland Trail Blazers, a team in a far less appealing market, sold for $4.25 billion. And though league officials stress that their cap proposal is motivated by a desire to give fans in smaller markets an equal shake, there's no denying that maximizing franchise values also is a major motivation.

In their eyes, the fact that the Minnesota Twins and Washington Nationals were taken off the market is just as telling, if not more so, than the Padres and Angels blowing away the market.

"If you're in Southern California, if you're in the San Francisco Bay Area, if you're the Yankees -- yeah, you're going to get a huge number," a source with extensive experience advising major league owners on sales said. "But good luck being the Kansas City Royals. Or the Cleveland [Guardians]. Or the Detroit Tigers. I mean seriously. There's a huge split in asset values."

With the Angels, Kroenke essentially purchased a blank canvas -- one with no debt, few payroll obligations and the potential for a new ballpark. With the Padres, Jones and Feliciano purchased a relatively finished product -- one with a potentially onerous future.

The Padres have a bloated payroll, with a combined $810 million still owed to Machado, Fernando Tatis Jr., Xander Bogaerts and Jackson Merrill after this season. Seven years from now, in 2033, the four of them will still be owed $116 million. By that point, Machado and Bogaerts will be playing in their age-40 seasons.

"It's going to get ugly," a rival general manager said of the Padres' future payroll obligations.

Some would argue it already is. Machado, Tatis, Bogaerts and Merrill absorbing an outsized portion of the Padres' commitments has prompted longtime GM A.J. Preller to supplement the team's depth on the trade front, continually drying up the Padres' farm system in the process. ESPN's Kiley McDaniel ranked them last going into this season.

Preller is widely considered as good as anyone in the industry at developing coveted prospects. In recent years, he has also excelled at finding production from players who have been cast aside elsewhere, namely Ty France, Gavin Sheets, Dustin Harris, Walker Buehler and Jeremiah Estrada. If not for them, the Padres would be teetering. Every year, rival front office executives believe, the Padres' margin for error only seems to diminish.

"To me, those are all opportunities," Feliciano said when asked how he viewed the pros and cons of his investment in the franchise. "Look at how much we have accomplished -- how much this team has accomplished, being from a small market and all those things. To me, the theme is that we've been able to exceed expectations. And we have been able to surprise people."

People in league circles would argue it's a surprise because what they've done is not realistic. Not without operating under losses, which prompted the Padres to take out a $50 million loan to address short-term cash-flow shortages and cover player payroll commitments in September 2023, as first reported by The Athletic. Not without being run by someone like Cohen, whose net worth is at least three times greater than that of 26 other owners, according to Forbes.

So, maybe the Padres are an outlier. Maybe they're a cautionary tale. Or maybe they're a shining example -- a reflection of what's possible with the right intentions.

To the people inside the organization, all that matters is that, someday, for the first time, they're champions.

"We've been so internally focused on what we're trying to accomplish here, in what we've been trying to grow here, that we'll leave it to those outside the organization that may have an opinion on what that means to the industry," Greupner said. "For us, we want to win a World Series championship. We've been trying to win in business and baseball in a way that can lead to that outcome."

stories.headline: NBA Rank 2026, players Nos. 50-11: Where LeBron, Steph, KD check in
stories.summary: Our countdown of the NBA's top 100 players continues. See which stars just missed a spot in the top 10 -- and where three legends land.
stories.body:
NBA Rank is back! With less than one month until opening night, let's continue counting down the league's best players for 2026-27.

After unveiling players Nos. 100-51 on Tuesday, our rankings now enter the top 50. It's a group headlined by former MVPs, future first-ballot Hall of Famers and young stars expected to take major leaps this season.

It's also where LeBron James checks in, his first time outside the top 10 in NBA Rank's 15-year history. (You can jump to LeBron's NBA Rank here.)

The rankings rollout concludes Thursday with our expert panel's top 10 players. And that panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition.

In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list. That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list, which features plenty of superstars who just missed our top 10.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

50. Dylan Harper
G | San Antonio Spurs

Age: 20

2025 NBA Rank: NR

The youngest member of the Spurs was the one who seemed to rise highest in the altitude of the Finals and stands to make a big jump in Year 2, whether he stays coming off the bench or makes the leap to the first five. He will earn more respect from the officials (1.7 free throw attempts in 69 games as a rookie), take a bigger role in the offense and improve on his already-respectable playmaking. Harper is an All-Star in the making. -- Vincent Goodwill

Signature stat: Harper had six games with at least 15 points and 65% shooting from the field in the 2026 playoffs, the most by a guard in NBA postseason history.

Fantasy projection: 15.2 PTS, 5.0 AST, 4.4 REB

49. Lauri Markkanen
F | Utah Jazz

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 43

Markkanen, a scoring forward who can stretch the court, has languished as a forgotten man in Utah. The Finnish star's competence often came into conflict with the Jazz's desire to improve their draft positioning during a multiyear rebuilding effort, and he has appeared in only one game in April over the past four seasons. Though his contract is overly generous for a player lacking All-NBA credentials, Markkanen should benefit from Utah's recent talent upgrades as he eyes his first career postseason appearance. -- Ben Golliver

Signature stat: Markkanen has nine seasons with at least 100 3-pointers, tied with Karl-Anthony Towns and Dirk Nowitzki for the most by a 7-footer in NBA history.

Fantasy projection: 23.8 PTS, 7.2 REB, 1.9 AST

48. Kon Knueppel
G | Charlotte Hornets

Age: 21

2025 NBA Rank: NR

Knueppel had a historic debut season. He finished second for Rookie of the Year behind a rookie-record, Hornets-record and NBA season-high 273 made 3-pointers. There will be change for Knueppel this upcoming season, as LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges are both gone. Ball assisted on 73 of Knueppel's 3s last season, the fourth most by any passer-scorer combination. Bridges assisted on 49, the second most on the team. -- Matt Williams

Signature stat: Knueppel was the first rookie to lead the NBA in made 3-pointers (272). Prior to last season, no first-year player had ever finished in the top three.

Fantasy projection: 20.0 PTS, 5.8 REB, 3.7 AST

47. Derrick White
G | Boston Celtics

Age: 32

2025 NBA Rank: 26

An inconsistent season on offense has White sliding back twenty-one spots. White continues to be one of the league's best defenders but an inconsistent season on offense has him sliding back 21 spots. For the first time in his career, White shot less than 40% from the field. In the playoffs, White's points per game decreased from 16.5 in the regular season to 8.7 in the first round. He shot 30.9% from the field and 26.5% on 3s. With Jaylen Brown traded to Philadelphia, the Celtics need consistency from White to contend in the revamped Eastern Conference. White has three years and $98 million remaining on his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Signature stat: Among qualified players, White saw the largest drop in effective field goal percentage from 2024-25 to 2025-26.

Fantasy projection: 16.6 PTS, 5.3 AST, 1.2 BLK

46. Brandon Miller
F | Charlotte Hornets

Age: 23

2025 NBA Rank: 76

Charlotte's deals with Minnesota (LaMelo Ball) and Phoenix (Miles Bridges) weren't just signals of a change in the franchise's direction, but they were a tacit endorsement of Miller. Selected No. 2 in 2023, the 6-7 forward is a proven scorer (19.0 points per game for his career) and made strides in his efficiency last season by setting personal bests in accuracy from 3 (38.3%) and the foul line (89.2%). -- Dave McMenamin

Signature stat: Led Hornets with 20.2 PPG last season

Fantasy projection: 22.3 PTS, 5.4 REB, 3.7 AST

45. Franz Wagner
F | Orlando Magic

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 32

Wagner is a talented shooter-scorer on the wing whose 6-10 size makes him a nightly mismatch. The main thing standing between Wagner and his first All-Star selection has been health, with him playing only 94 of a possible 162 games the past two seasons. But Wagner has averaged 22.9 points per game in that span and matches with Paolo Banchero and Desmond Bane to give the Magic one of the most formidable 2-3-4 combos in the NBA. -- André Snellings

Signature stat: Orlando went 20-14 in Wagner's career-low 34 games played last season (25-23 without).

Fantasy projection: 22.5 PTS, 5.7 REB. 4.2 AST

44. Trae Young
G | Washington Wizards

Age: 27

2025 NBA Rank: 29

Other than finagling his way to a new four-year, $212.8 million contract -- a huge win, to be fair -- the past year was one to forget for Young. He played only 15 games due to injuries and was traded to the team with the worst record in the league. Meanwhile, the Hawks took off in the standings after dealing him.

In his first full season as a Wizard, Young will surely do his part to boost an offense that ranked 29th in efficiency last year, but he won't help a defense that ranked 30th. One major question for Washington is how much Young dominates on the ball, versus occasionally spacing the floor and deferring to the Wizards' young playmakers on the perimeter. -- Kram

Signature stat: Young, Oscar Robertson, LeBron James and Nikola Jokic are the only players in NBA history with at least 25 points and 10 assists per game in consecutive seasons.

Fantasy projection: 23.8 PTS, 10.8 AST, 1.2 STL

43. De'Aaron Fox
G | San Antonio Spurs

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: 35

Fox smoothly downshifted into his new life as Wembanyama's sidekick in their first full season together, but the 6-foot-3 guard's poor play in the Finals led critics to call for him to be benched or traded. San Antonio stood by Fox this summer, opting to keep the two-time All-Star and the bulk of its 62-win team intact. However, the scrutiny on Fox will only intensify with 2025 lottery pick Dylan Harper eyeing an expanded role. Fox's unsightly 41/29/76 shooting splits in the 2026 playoffs simply must improve for the Spurs to fulfill their championship dreams. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Fox ranks fourth in clutch time points since entering the league in 2017-18, behind DeMar DeRozan, LeBron James and Nikola Jokic.

Fantasy projection: 20.6 PTS, 5.6 AST, 1.4 STL

42. Rudy Gobert
C | Minnesota Timberwolves

Age: 34

2025 NBA Rank: 49

The Timberwolves ranked eighth in defensive efficiency last season, but their success varied depending on the presence of Gobert. When he was on the floor, they had a 108.0 defensive rating. That rose to 115.9 when Gobert was on the bench. But the intriguing part of Gobert's game this season will be his partnership with LaMelo Ball in the pick-and-roll. Ball ranked second in on-ball screens as the ball handler last season, while Gobert was third in picks set as the screener, according to GeniusIQ player tracking. -- Williams

Signature stat: Gobert's four Defensive Player of the Year awards are tied for the most in NBA history with Dikembe Mutombo and Ben Wallace.

Fantasy projection: 11.9 PTS, 11.7 REB, 1.7 BLK

41. Joel Embiid
C | Philadelphia 76ers

Age: 32

2025 NBA Rank: 47

When Embiid plays, he's productive and must be accounted for on every scouting report -- a shoo-in for 27 points and eight boards and a matchup nightmare with his ability to score at all three levels. But "when he plays" is still an issue, the biggest question mark for whether this talent-laden 76ers experiment can lead to a run through May. Since winning MVP in 2023, he has played in a possible 96 of 246 games (39%). -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Embiid has averaged 27.64 points per game throughout his career, fourth most in NBA history and second most by a frontcourt player (Wilt Chamberlain: 30.07).

Fantasy projection: 27.4 PTS, 8.2 REB, 1.2 BLK

40. Anthony Davis
F | Washington Wizards

Age: 33

2025 NBA Rank: 14

It has been a disastrous couple of seasons for Davis since his shocking trade from the Lakers to the Mavericks. He has appeared in just 29 games since late-January 2025 and was traded a second time to the Wizards in February. Davis has yet to play for Washington due to a hand injury but enters 2026-27 fully healthy, and his on-court performance this season will be key to his long-term future after Davis' representatives and the Wizards shelved extension talks this summer. He's owed $58.5 million this season and has a $62.8 million player option for 2027-28. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Davis is one of 11 players to average 20 points and 10 rebounds per game in at least 10 seasons. The only other player among the 11 to have played in 21st century is Shaquille O'Neal, with a league-record 13 20-10 seasons.

Fantasy projection: 22.6 PTS, 11.4 REB, 2.1 BLK

39. Kyrie Irving
G | Dallas Mavericks

Age: 34

2025 NBA Rank: NR (injury)

Irving was 25th two years ago but dropped out of the top 100 while recovering from a torn right ACL. The 34-year-old has averaged at least 20 points per game in nine straight seasons and rejoins a revamped Maverick roster featuring Cooper Flagg and new coach Dusty May. A healthy Irving will improve an offense that ranked 22nd in assists and 29th in 3-pointers made. Irving has two years left on his contract, including a player option in 2027-28, and could be a trade candidate if Dallas is out of playoff contention by February. -- Marks

Signature stat: Irving, who has routinely flirted with shooting splits of 50% from the field, 40% from 3 and 90% from the free throw line, pulled off the feat in 2020-21. He is one of three players in NBA history with a 50/40/90 season on at least 20 shots per game (Stephen Curry in 2015-16, Larry Bird in 1986-87 and 1987-88).

Fantasy projection: 24.6 PTS, 4.8 AST, 1.3 STL

38. Stephon Castle
G | San Antonio Spurs

Age: 21

2025 NBA Rank: 99

Castle raised his game in every way as a sophomore. He was a dominant defender coming out of college, with the size and strength of a big wing but with the quickness and tenacity to lock up opposing point guards. Castle's offensive game is developing as he improves as both a shooter and a distributor, both skills building from his natural ability to get to the rim off the dribble. Castle joins Wembanyama and Harper as the young, supremely talented nucleus of a Spurs team that seems destined for many more Finals trips. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Last season, Castle became the youngest player in NBA history to record at least 40 points, 12 rebounds, and 12 assists in game.

Fantasy projection: 18.1 PTS, 7.6 AST, 5.6 REB

37. Austin Reaves
G | Los Angeles Lakers

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: 60

Reaves' dream season was cut short in April by an oblique injury that, paired with Luka Doncic's hamstring strain, helped derail the Lakers' postseason. He was still rewarded with a four-year, $180 million extension to stay in L.A. and build the next era with Doncic after LeBron James' departure to the 76ers in free agency. The 6-5 combo guard has shown his ability to make plays for himself and others at a high level. The next step in him reaching All-Star status will be his continued improvement defensively and having health on his side like in 2023-24 when he played all 82 games. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Reaves is one of two undrafted players to sign a $100 million NBA contract, along with fellow Wichita State alum Fred VanVleet.

Fantasy projection: 23.4 PTS, 5.9 AST, 4.9 REB

36. Paolo Banchero
F | Orlando Magic

Age: 23

2025 NBA Rank: 17

Banchero is an imposing forward whose stock has taken a slight hit due to his inability to smooth out his rough edges. While the 2022 No. 1 overall pick has regularly stuffed the stat sheet and led the Magic to three straight playoff appearances, he has also collected naysayers who decry his anachronistic shot selection and choppy decision-making. Banchero ranked 33rd in true shooting percentage out of the 42 players who attempted at least 1,000 shots last season, and the Magic have never ranked higher than 18th in offensive efficiency during his career. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Last season, Banchero joined Luka Doncic as the only players to score at least 35 points in their first two career Game 7s.

Fantasy projection: 23.4 PTS, 7.9 REB, 5.2 AST

35. LaMelo Ball
G | Minnesota Timberwolves

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 63

The Timberwolves needed a point guard and additional creator next to Anthony Edwards and they got that in Ball. Health had been an issue over the past few seasons, but Ball played 72 games in 2025-26, his most since 2021-22 (75). And despite a career low in minutes, Ball ranked second in made 3-pointers and was one of eight players to average 20 points and seven assists per game. -- Williams

Signature stat: Ball averages 3.22 made 3-pointers per game for his career, the second most in NBA history among players with at least 300 games played. (Stephen Curry's 3.97 per game is first.)

Fantasy projection: 23.1 PTS, 8.0 AST, 5.4 REB

34. OG Anunoby
F | New York Knicks

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 41

It all came together for Anunoby last postseason. One of the league's most consistent players, despite never making an All-Star team, stepped into the forefront. That tip-in in Game 4 of the Finals was one of the biggest baskets in Madison Square Garden history, and he'll be royalty forever for it. Quietly, though, he might've been the Knicks' second-best player in the postseason (20.1 points on ridiculous 56/49/85 splits) while still playing lockdown defense. He'll be tasked with guarding wings and bigs as the Knicks try to repeat. -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Anunoby joined Walt Frazier and Bernard King as only Knicks players to average at least 20 points, five rebounds and 55% shooting in the postseason.

Fantasy projection: 16.9 PTS, 5.2 REB, 1.5 STL

33. Jalen Duren
C | Detroit Pistons (restricted FA)

Age: 22

2025 NBA Rank: NR

An All-NBA season puts Duren in the top 35 for the first time, but questions remain despite last year's regular-season success. First, will the contract stalemate end before the start of training camp or will Duren play out this season on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer? The deadline to sign the offer is Oct. 1. Second, will Duren's postseason struggles carry over? In the 2026 playoffs, Duren averaged 10.1 points per game, the second-largest scoring decrease from the regular season to the postseason in NBA history, according to ESPN Research. -- Marks

Signature stat: Last season, Duren became the first Piston to average at least 15 points, 10 rebounds and 60% shooting from the field.

Fantasy projection: 20.3 PTS, 11.7 REB, 1.0 BLK

32. James Harden
G | Cleveland Cavaliers

Age: 37

2025 NBA Rank: 23

In many ways, Harden remains the same player now, in his late 30s, as he was half a decade ago, or even to some extent in his prime. He always orchestrates efficient offenses. He takes (and makes) smart shots and still generates gobs of free throws. And he's an indifferent defender at the best of times.

After a midseason trade to Cleveland, Harden meshed well with Donovan Mitchell, as the Cavaliers posted a 126.4 offensive rating with that duo on the floor, per databallr. Cleveland is hoping for more of the same, or an even better performance, in their first full season together. -- Kram

Signature stat: Harden has seven seasons with at least 20 points and 8 assists per game, tied with Oscar Robertson (10) for second all-time.

Fantasy projection: 20.6 PTS, 8.1 AST, 5.0 REB

31. Amen Thompson
F | Houston Rockets

Age: 23

2025 NBA Rank: 37

At 6-7 with a sturdy frame and explosive leaping ability, Thompson profiled as a prototypical 3-and-D wing. But his offensive game has developed rapidly in each of his three seasons, allowing him to play a lot of point forward with his ability to penetrate off the dribble and break down opposing defenses with an eye for playmaking. Thompson is the basketball equivalent of a five-tool prospect who is growing into a franchise centerpiece. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Thompson and Cleveland's Evan Mobley were the only players with at least 200 dunks last season. Thompson's 201 dunks were the most by a player shorter than 6-10 since Montrezl Harrell in 2018-19 (203).

Fantasy projection: 17.7 PTS, 7.7 REB, 5.1 AST, 1.5 STL

30. Alperen Sengun
C | Houston Rockets

Age: 24

2025 NBA Rank: 25

In Houston's first game last season, Sengun made a career-high five 3-pointers against the Thunder; it seemed as if he was poised to take a leap. But the rest of the season didn't quite work out that way, as Sengun finished with essentially the same numbers as he has in every recent season. For instance, his player efficiency rating has been 22.0, 21.4 and 21.4 over the past three years.

Those numbers are still sufficient to make Sengun an All-Star, but not the primary option on a contender. Combine that offensive plateau with a minor step back defensively, and Sengun's ceiling looks lower now than it did a year ago. -- Kram

Signature stat: Sengun, Oscar Robertson and Luka Doncic are the only players in NBA history to average 20 points, eight rebounds and five assists in multiple seasons before turning 24 years old.

Fantasy projection: 20.0 PTS, 9.4 REB, 5.7 AST

29. Pascal Siakam
F | Indiana Pacers

Age: 32

2025 NBA Rank: 22

Siakam was the lone bright spot in a miserable Pacers season following Tyrese Haliburton's injury in the 2025 NBA Finals. He made the All-Star team and put up the second-highest scoring average in his career on higher volume. This season, Haliburton returns and Siakam returns to his role as co-star on a team that has designs on getting back to the NBA Finals. At 32 years old, his game should still be highly effective, and at times he can be a potent scorer (14 games of 30 points or more). -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Siakam is one of three players with at least 2,000 minutes and 1,000 points in each of the past eight seasons (DeMar DeRozan, Nikola Jokic).

Fantasy projection: 22.8 PTS, 7.3 REB, 4.0 AST

28. Bam Adebayo
C | Miami Heat

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 21

Last season, Adebayo joined Shaquille O'Neal and Alonzo Mourning as the only Heat players to average 20 points and 10 rebounds in a season. The highlight of Adebayo's campaign came on March 10, when he scored 83 points, the second most in a game in NBA history. The next chapter in his Heat career pairs him with Giannis Antetokounmpo. The two-time MVP and former Buck has experience playing with floor-spacing centers, and Adebayo can provide the same help in Miami. He attempted 400 3-pointers last season, more than his first eight seasons combined. -- Williams

Signature stat: Adebayo's 83-point night was the highest scoring game since Wilt Chamberlain's 100 in March 1962.

Fantasy projection: 20.2 PTS, 10.0 REB, 1.2 STL

27. Deni Avdija
F | Portland Trail Blazers

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 66

Few observers saw Avdija's rapid ascension coming when the Blazers acquired him from the Wizards in a largely overlooked 2024 trade. The punishing wing enjoyed a breakout 2025-26 campaign, posting career highs in scoring, player efficiency rating and win shares while earning his first All-Star selection and leading Portland to the playoffs for the first time in five years. There's more good news: Avdija projects as one of the NBA's best values in 2026-27 given that his bargain $13.1 million salary is less than the midlevel exception. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Avdija finished fourth in NBA in drawing fouls last season, but he was at his best drawing contact in the paint. Avdija drew 267 fouls in the paint, second in the NBA behind Paolo Banchero (275), per Genius IQ.

Fantasy projection: 23.0 PTS, 7.2 REB, 6.3 AST

26. Evan Mobley
F | Cleveland Cavaliers

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 13

The Cavaliers extended Donovan Mitchell, re-signed James Harden and traded for Peyton Watson. But the wild card in how far the Cavaliers go this season could become Mobley. Named Defensive Player of the Year in 2025 (he was also named All-NBA second team), Mobley saw a small dip on the defensive end and regressed offensively. The Cavaliers were plus-5.9 points per 100 possessions with Mobley on the court in the regular season but nearly 10 points worse in the postseason. -- Marks

Signature stat: Since entering the league in 2022, Mobley is one of six players with 400 blocks and 200 steals.

Fantasy projection: 18.9 PTS, 9.8 REB, 1.7 BLK

25. Jalen Williams
G | Oklahoma City Thunder

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 11

Injuries sabotaged Williams' 2025-26 season and ultimately could be the No. 1 reason why we're not talking about the Thunder as back-to-back champs. First, offseason wrist surgery following the title over Indiana caused Williams to miss 19 games to start the regular season, then hamstring strains to both legs sidelined him for most of the postseason. Still only 25, the 6-5 Williams is a three-level scorer who commits on the defensive end. His 3-point accuracy will be an X factor for him this season. He shot 42.7% from deep in 2023-24 but just 29.9% in limited action last year. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Injuries limited Williams to a career-low 33 games last season, and he played in just five of Thunder's 15 playoff games.

Fantasy projection: 20.6 PTS, 5.3 AST, 1.4 STL

24. Chet Holmgren
C | Oklahoma City Thunder

Age: 24

2025 NBA Rank: 24

Holmgren has the length and timing as a shot blocker to make him the best defender of his generation outside of Wembanyama. Holmgren also has the shooting touch and quickness off the dribble to make him a mismatch for most opposing big men to defend. Holmgren's skill set is so strong, in fact, that the biggest criticism he faces is that he isn't aggressive enough on offense to take advantage of those mismatches. Holmgren remains a pillar for the Thunder, but a shift in offensive mindset could put him on the brink of superstardom. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Last season, Holmgren set career highs in points per game (17.1), rebounds per game (8.9) and field goal percentage (56%).

Fantasy projection: 16.5 PTS, 8.4 REB, 2.1 BLK

23. Cooper Flagg
F | Dallas Mavericks

Age: 19

2025 NBA Rank: 52

Flagg's rookie season began with a whimper, as he struggled to adjust to the NBA while being thrust into the unfamiliar position of point guard. But it ended with a bang at his rightful position of small forward, as a torrid late-season burst -- including back-to-back games with 51 and 45 points in April -- propelled him to his expected Rookie of the Year honor.

The former No. 1 pick doesn't even celebrate his 20th birthday until December, yet he's already one of the best two-way wings in the league, with a strong defensive foundation and a budding offensive skill set. Flagg must improve his jump shot (29.5% on 3s last year), but that might be the only real obstacle standing in the way of an All-Star berth. -- Kram

Signature stat: Flagg is the first teenager in NBA history to record a 50-point game.

Fantasy projection: 22.3 PTS, 7.0 REB, 4.8 AST

22. Jalen Johnson
F | Atlanta Hawks

Age: 24

2025 NBA Rank: 44

The Hawks clearly made the right call by passing the torch from Trae Young to Johnson, who earned his first All-Star selection with an absurdly productive 2025-26 season. The 6-8 forward thrived as a playmaker and finisher in Atlanta's up-tempo attack, and he helped lead the franchise to its most wins since 2015-16. What's more, his plus-3.2 net rating surpassed Young's best mark in any of the previous four seasons. To climb even further up these rankings, the 24-year-old Johnson must prove his game can fully translate to the postseason after an underwhelming series against the Knicks. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Johnson's 13 triple-doubles last season set the Hawks franchise record.

Fantasy projection: 23.0 PTS, 10.6 REB, 7.9 AST

21. Jamal Murray
G | Denver Nuggets

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 46

Murray had one of the bigger jumps in the rankings after being named an All-Star and making All-NBA for the first time in his career. He was the only player to average at least 25 points, seven assists and 40% on 3-pointers in 2025-26. Murray also finished second for Clutch Player of the Year after ranking top two in clutch time points and assists. -- Williams

Signature stat: Last season, Murray set career highs in points per game (25.4), assists per game (7.1) and 3-pointers made (245).

Fantasy projection: 23.1 PTS, 6.6 AST, 4.1 REB

20. Devin Booker
G | Phoenix Suns

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 16

Booker is one of the most malleable stars as the Suns have assembled various teams around him in recent years and yet, he continues to thrive. From teaming with Chris Paul to playing alongside Kevin Durant to now, having Dillon Brooks as a running mate. Pencil him in for 26 points and 6 assists, the ability to play both guard positions and playing through nicks and bruises. His 11 years in the league have been in the Valley, and he's signed through 2029-30 -- a rare one-team star. -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Booker was one of five players with at least 1,000 drives last season and was one of eight players to score 1,000 points when he drove (min. 500 drives), per Genius IQ tracking.

Fantasy projection: 26.5 PTS, 6.7 AST, 4.2 REB

19. Tyrese Haliburton
G | Indiana Pacers

Age: 26

2025 NBA Rank: NR (injury)

Haliburton would have been in the top 15 last year had he not suffered a torn Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. On the sidelines for all last season, Haliburton witnessed one of the best offenses plummet in all statistical categories. The Pacers ranked 27th in offensive efficiency, 26th in field goal percentage, 20th in 3-point percentage and 18th in fast-break points. -- Marks

Signature stat: Haliburton has the second-best assist-to-turnover ratio (3.81) in NBA postseason history (min. 300 assists) since individual turnovers were first tracked in 1977-78 (John Paxson, 4.31).

Fantasy projection: 19.2 PTS, 9.9 AST, 1.3 STL

18. LeBron James
F | Philadelphia 76ers

Age: 41

2025 NBA Rank: 8

Seeing James outside the top 10 is jarring. Then again, seeing a guy who turns 42 in a few months still inside the top 25 is probably the better framing to appreciate what the 22-time All-Star continues to accomplish. James already had success as L.A.'s No. 3 option last season and will likely reprise that role behind Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown for the 76ers. The difference is that while James' scoring took a back seat to Doncic and Reaves for the Lakers, his touches might not suffer too much in Philly. Sixers president of basketball operations Mike Gansey has indicated the team will have James play point forward and orchestrate the offense, similar to his role with the Lakers when they won the 2020 title. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: The 41-year-old James finished second in the NBA in fast-break points last season, behind only his new teammate, Tyrese Maxey.

Fantasy projection: 21.0 PTS, 7.0 AST, 6.3 REB

17. Scottie Barnes
F | Toronto Raptors

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 30

Barnes has developed from the 2022 Rookie of the Year to a two-time All-Star entering his sixth season. He has been the do-everything engine for the Raptors on both offense and defense, finishing fifth in the Defensive Player of the Year vote while leading the team in assists and scoring nearly 20 points per game. This season he will join Kawhi Leonard as the nucleus of a Raptors squad that is trying to make the leap from play-in scrappy competitors to playoffs contenders. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Barnes led his team in rebounds, assists, steals and blocks last season. Since 2017-18, LeBron James (2021-22) and Nikola Jokic (2017-18) are the only other players to accomplish the feat.

Fantasy projection: 18.8 PTS, 7.7 REB, 6.0 AST, 1.4 STL

16. Karl-Anthony Towns
C | New York Knicks

Age: 30

2025 NBA Rank: 27

Few players saw their reputations rise as high last season as Towns. Throughout his career, the former No. 1 pick had been dogged by criticisms of his foolish mistakes -- costly turnovers, silly fouls -- and even in the middle of last season, drama swirled about his role in New York's offense under coach Mike Brown.

But that all changed during a magical playoff run, in which Towns made 46% of his 3-point attempts and played the best, most consistent defense of his career en route to a title. He only averaged 16 points during the playoffs, but he was a picture-perfect role player. With Mitchell Robinson gone to Boston in free agency, the Knicks don't have much of a Plan B if Towns' struggles at center return. But he more than proved himself in the postseason. -- Kram

Signature stat: During the Knicks' run to the 2026 title, Towns became the first player in NBA postseason history to record 55/45/90 shooting splits with least 400 minutes played.

Fantasy projection: 21.9 PTS, 11.2 REB, 4.4 AST

15. Kawhi Leonard
F | Toronto Raptors

Age: 35

2025 NBA Rank: 20

Leonard flew the coop to Canada after his seven-season run with the Clippers ended in infamy. While the seven-time All-Star escaped the NBA's salary cap circumvention investigation with only a $700,000 fine, his Raptors reunion will reportedly play out under the cloud of a separate federal investigation. On the court, Leonard posted career highs in points and player efficiency rating last season -- a remarkable feat considering he turned 35 in June. Toronto's young roster should benefit from his championship experience, but Leonard, who hasn't advanced past the first round since 2021, must prove he can still crank it up in the playoffs. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Leonard, who set a career high with 27.9 points per game last season, scored at least 20 in each of his final 57 games for the Clippers. That tied Bob McAdoo for the longest streak in franchise history.

Fantasy projection: 25.1 PTS, 6.2 REB, 1.7 STL

14. Jaylen Brown
F | Philadelphia 76ers

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 19

With Jayson Tatum missing most of the 2025-26 season, Brown posted the third-highest usage rate in the league behind Doncic and Antetokounmpo. He delivered in those minutes, averaging 28.7 points, the fifth most in a season in Celtics history. In addition, Brown became the fourth Celtics player to average 25 points, five rebounds and five assists in a season in franchise history, joining Tatum, Larry Bird and John Havlicek. But the move to the 76ers opens questions about what his usage looks like playing alongside James, Embiid and Maxey. -- Williams

Signature stat: Last season, Brown set career highs in points (28.7), rebounds (6.9), and assists (5.1) per game.

Fantasy projection: 23.9 PTS, 5.9 REB, 4.3 AST

13. Kevin Durant
F | Houston Rockets

Age: 37

2025 NBA Rank: 9

For all the talk of the ageless wonders in the NBA, 38-year-old (on 9/29) Kevin Durant doesn't quite fly under the radar, but his longevity feels somewhat underappreciated. He made the All-NBA team for the 12th time, tied for seventh in the history of the league with the likes of Dirk Nowitzki, Hakeem Olajuwon and Jerry West, among others. Since his right Achilles injury in 2019, he has averaged 27/6/5 on 53/41/88 splits. He helped keep the Rockets afloat in his first season, but they flamed out in the first round against the Lakers. Durant is a leader by example, and this seemed to conflict with the youth on the roster at times. Do the Rockets have enough leadership, and will he have enough gas in a top-heavy West? -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Durant enters 2026-27 on a four-season streak of at least 25 points per game, 50% shooting from the field and 40% shooting from 3. No other player has more than three such seasons for their career.

Fantasy projection: 25.0 PTS, 5.6 REB, 4.4 AST

12. Stephen Curry
G | Golden State Warriors

Age: 38

2025 NBA Rank: 7

Durability concerns have Curry falling out of the top 10. After missing most of the 2025 second round with a hamstring injury, Curry played the third-fewest games of his career in 2025-26. (He missed 29 games after Jan. 24 with a right knee injury.) Managing Curry's minutes will be key even with Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody out an extended period. Last season, he averaged his fewest minutes of the past six seasons. The 38-year-old is eligible to sign up to a two-year, $137 million extension. -- Marks

Signature stat: Curry has 26,528 career points with Warriors, third most with a single franchise in NBA history behind Kobe Bryant (33,643 with Lakers) and Dirk Nowitzki (31,560 with Mavericks).

Fantasy projection: 25.8 PTS, 5.3 AST, 4.2 REB, 4.6 3PM

11. Tyrese Maxey
G | Philadelphia 76ers

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 28

Maxey's scoring average has increased in each of his six seasons in the league, topping out at 28.3 points per game last season (No. 5 in the league) to earn him an All-NBA third team selection. It cannot be overstated how much Maxey's presence factored into LeBron James' decision to sign with the 76ers, and it will be on the 25-year-old combo guard to make James and Jaylen Brown feel welcome, while still maximizing the holdover talents of Embiid and VJ Edgecombe. There's nothing about Maxey's game or personality that would suggest that he won't be able to continue to thrive with the spotlight even brighter this season. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Maxey has increased his points per game and 3-point percentage in each season of his NBA career.

stories.headline: Liverpool close to appointing Julian Ward as sporting director - sources
stories.summary: Liverpool are closing in on the appointment of Julian Ward as the club's new sporting director, sources told ESPN.
stories.body:
Liverpool are closing in on the appointment of Julian Ward as the club's new sporting director, sources told ESPN.

Ward previously held the position for the duration of the 2022-23 season and is now set to take up the role for a second time following the departure of Richard Hughes. Hughes joined Liverpool from AFC Bournemouth in March 2024 and was tasked with leading the rebuild following the departure of manager Jürgen Klopp.

The Scot appointed both Arne Slot and his successor Andoni Iraola before leaving the club earlier this month to take up a new role at Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal. The search for his successor has been led by Fenway Sports Group (FSG) president Mike Gordon, with internal candidate Ward quickly emerging as the frontrunner.

Ward has spent the past two years working as FSG's technical director, having previously left Liverpool in 2023. During his time as the Reds' sporting director, he oversaw the signings of players such as Darwin Núñez, Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo before stepping down for personal reasons.

His association with the club dates back to 2012, when he joined from Manchester City to oversee the club's scouting network in Spain and Portugal. Over the next decade, he went on to assume a number of roles in the Reds' football operations department, including loan pathways and football partnerships manager and assistant sporting director to Michael Edwards.

His reappointment as sporting director is expected to offer some continuity for Liverpool behind the scenes at a time when the 1892 Holdings Consortium -- led by Amit Bhatia and including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos -- are in the process of buying a 38% stake in the club.

stories.headline: Why Aaron Glenn is encouraged by the Jets' progress
stories.summary: New York is an overtime loss away from being undefeated after allowing the fewest yards through two weeks.
stories.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- Perhaps the strongest endorsement for New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn came more than a year ago, delivered by his previous boss.

"If he can't [turn them around]," Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said at the 2025 NFL spring meetings in Orlando, "nobody can."

Despite a firestorm of criticism in the aftermath of the 20-17 overtime loss to the Green Bay Packers, Glenn has the Jets looking like a competitive team so far in his second season. It's overshadowed by a handful of questionable coaching decisions from the fourth quarter collapse Sunday, but he is encouraged by the progress and insisted they won't allow the crushing loss to define their season.

Glenn can prevent that from happening by beating the next opponent, which happens to be -- drum roll, please -- Campbell and the Lions. It's a delicious storyline, but Glenn, who served as Campbell's defensive coordinator from 2021 to 2024, can't let that distract him. His primary job is to re-focus his team after blowing a 10-point lead.

"It's my responsibility to get our guys to be able to close the door," Glenn said. "I take that, and it's something I will never run from."

There are some positives to build on, which should make it easier to move past the Green Bay debacle. In two games, the Jets already have run more plays with a lead (68) than they did the entire 2025 season (66). They dominated the Tennessee Titans in the opener, never trailing, and they were only one timely play away from burying the Packers.

The Jets have their best total yardage margin (+258) through two games since 1982, currently the third-best margin in the NFL. The defense, with Glenn calling the plays, is ranked No. 1 in yards allowed (197 per game). They have surrendered only 30 points, including 20 in the fourth quarter and overtime -- perhaps a troubling trend.

Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips said they will make "a conscious effort this week to step up the intensity" in the latter portion of practice, hoping there's a carryover to the game.

The Jets allowed the Packers to score on three of their last four possessions. Before that, they held Green Bay's vertical passing attack in check, though some of that could be attributed to Jordan Love's reliance on short passing because of a spate of offensive line injuries.

The takeaway-starved defense, which has gone a record 19 consecutive games without an interception, recorded its first takeaway of the season -- a fumble recovery. There could've been more, but they recovered only one of five fumbles by the Packers.

Glenn took that as a positive, saying, "We're attacking the football. We're punching the football out and I do know this: Those things are going to come around for us."

Offensively, the Jets haven't put up big numbers (40 points), but they're getting consistent quarterback play -- something that didn't happen last season. Geno Smith, who threw an NFL-high 17 interceptions last season for the Las Vegas Raiders, has yet to commit a turnover. Ditto, the entire offense -- the first time since 1971 they've had no giveaways through the first two games.

"I still think we have a really good team, a team of high potential and we just went into a shootout with a [2025] playoff team," running back Breece Hall said after Sunday's game. "So I think we have everything we need."

It wasn't exactly a shootout, but there's no doubt the Jets have been better than last season on offense. Smith already has more passing yards in his first two starts (462) than Justin Fields recorded in his last four (460) from last season. They're still lacking explosive plays, so it might behoove offensive coordinator Frank Reich to get wide receiver Garrett Wilson more involved. Wilson was targeted only seven times on Sunday, just twice after his third-quarter touchdown.

"Absolutely, that's a point of emphasis every time we go out -- try to make sure we get him the ball, and we have to continue to do that," Glenn said. "There are guys on this team -- Breece, [Mason Taylor], [Kenyon Sadiq], especially Garrett -- that we have to make sure that we get those guys involved."

stories.body:
Lachie Neale has faced a monster media pack on arrival in Melbourne as the star Brisbane midfielder appeals his suspension for the AFL grand final.

Neale remains banned for Saturday's premiership decider against Fremantle after failing to argue his way out of a one-match suspension for a gut punch on Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan.

The dual Brownlow medallist gave a short statement after arriving at Melbourne Airport with Lions teammates on Wednesday.

"Very hopeful that it's successful, but regardless of the result, I'll be here to support the boys and the club," Neale said.

"It's a big week for the club."

Following the 15-second statement, Neale was chased by cameras as he immediately left the Virgin Australia terminal.

Fellow Lions veteran Dayne Zorko conducted a press conference after Neale's departure, with the majority of questions focused on the dual premiership co-captain.

Neale was also the story of grand final week last year, famously overcoming a calf injury to play a second-half cameo in Brisbane's demolition of Geelong.

"Lots of scrutiny last year about whether he'd play, whether he wouldn't," Zorko said.

"(20)24 he had a broken foot, so we're used to it.

"It's a lot (the attention), but he seems to be fine.

"I sat next to him on the plane.

"He's just taking it in his stride."

To succeed at an appeals board hearing on Thursday at 4pm, Brisbane will have to prove the tribunal finding was either an error of law, an unreasonable decision, a manifestly excessive classification, or a manifestly excessive sanction.

"There's been 10 (gut punch) incidents this year, all of them have resulted in a week (suspension)," the AFL's footy boss Greg Swann told reporters on Wednesday.

"That was the third (tribunal) appeal and they've all been upheld."

At the end of a four-and-a-half hour hearing on Tuesday night, the tribunal decided not to enact the 'exceptional and compelling clause' to allow Neale to avoid suspension.

Why? For many reasons, according to tribunal chair Jeff Gleeson KC.

There was Neale's evidence, which Gleeson rejected as "inconsistent".

Neale insisted he didn't strike Ginnivan during last Saturday night's preliminary final.

"We have listened carefully to Mr Neale's evidence but we find it was inconsistent in key respects with what we saw on the video," Gleeson said.

Neale maintained his shoulder and chest made contact with Ginnivan; the tribunal found it was "a forceful blow delivered with a swinging arm and an open hand".

That's the guilty part. Next was what Gleeson described as "the more difficult issue".

Was using the exceptional and compelling circumstances clause justified to downgrade Neale's penalty from a ban to a fine?

Introduced this year, the clause had been deployed once: to downgrade a one-game ban to Collingwood legend and the AFL's games record holder Scott Pendlebury, to a fine.

But Gleeson noted Pendlebury was charged with rough conduct. Specifically, graded as careless conduct, medium impact, and high contact.

Neale was charged with striking graded as intentional conduct, medium impact and body contact.

Then, there was Neale's record, which his barrister - the AFL's former football operations boss, Adrian Anderson - compared to Pendlebury.

Until Tuesday night, Neale had never been banned in a 15-year career including two Brownlow medals, six club champion awards, and captaining the Lions to two premierships.

stories.headline: Isack Hadjar signs Red Bull extension to race alongside Max Verstappen in 2027
stories.summary: Red Bull has confirmed Isack Hadjar will remain as one of its race drivers in 2027, completing the team's line-up alongside Max Verstappen.
stories.body:
Red Bull has confirmed Isack Hadjar will remain as one of its race drivers in 2027, completing the team's line-up alongside Max Verstappen.

Hadjar, who is returning to action at this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix after missing three races with a wrist injury, was promoted to Red Bull's senior team at the start of this year following a standout rookie season with Racing Bulls in 2025.

After multiple years of teammates struggling in Verstappen's shadow at Red Bull, Hadjar has made a solid start to his time at the team with eight finishes in the points and one podium at the Monaco Grand Prix.

At the Dutch Grand Prix in August, Red Bull put an end to months of speculation about Verstappen's future by announcing a new deal for the four-time world champion that will keep him at the team until the end of 2030.

Hadjar, who entered F1 through Red Bull's junior programme, is now confirmed as Verstappen's teammate for 2027.

"We're very excited to continue our journey with Isack," team principal Laurent Mekies said. "Since joining us at the start of the year, he has been superb on and off track, especially considering this is only his second Formula 1 season, which made extending his contract an easy decision.

"From the very beginning, Isack immersed himself in the team, spending every minute at the factory with his engineers to develop the car, always eager to learn and improve.

"You could see from that first weekend in Melbourne that he handled the step up with remarkable composure and had earned his place in this seat.

"The period since his injury has been a difficult one for Isack, but this extension is a testament to how much we believe in him and we can't wait to see him back out on track.

"We still have a lot we want to achieve this season, but it's a great feeling to know that the drivers, engineers and everyone back at the factory are all heading in the same direction, committed and together."

Hadjar added: "I am really excited to continue with Oracle Red Bull Racing. I came to this team eight months ago and immediately understood the scale and ambition of this organisation.

- Isack Hadjar returns to Red Bull for Azerbaijan GP after injury layoff

- Lando Norris backs 'exciting' 2027 Monaco GP sprint weekend but 'tougher for us drivers'

"There are so many talented people at the factory, and you're aware of the privilege of driving for such an incredible team alongside a four-time world champion like Max.

"From the moment I signed, I set out to dedicate myself to the team, and with the support of Laurent and everyone in Milton Keynes, I've been able to justify the faith they've had in me. I'm constantly looking to listen, learn and push myself further every single day, which only makes me more excited about what lies ahead."

Focus will now switch to the 2027 line-up of Red Bull's second team, Racing Bulls.

Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov is currently leading the Formula 2 championship with three rounds remaining and would make an obvious candidate to step up to F1 next year.

However, Racing Bulls incumbents Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad have both enjoyed strong seasons in F1 so far, leaving Red Bull with a tough decision over who to choose for 2027.

Lawson, who subbed in for Hadjar at Red Bull over the past three rounds, made his debut as a substitute for Daniel Ricciardo at the junior team in 2023, but is only in his second full season in F1 -- both of which have now included brief stints at Red Bull.

Lindblad is still in his rookie year and has impressed with ten points finishes from 14 rounds.

At the last round of the championship in Madrid, Racing Bull's team principal Alan Permane said his team was in no rush to make a decision on 2027.

"I think it's still too early for us," Permane said. "Frankly, we usually wait a bit longer. There's no pressure to announce our plans for next season just yet. "Nikola is definitely on our minds, and he's having an incredible season -- his debut in Formula 2, where he currently leads the championship. That said, Liam and Arvid are both fantastic drivers as well. It's a luxury problem."

If Racing Bulls opts to continue with its current line-up, one option could be for Tsolov to spend a year in the reserve driver role currently occupied by Yuki Tsunoda.

stories.headline: Burton, Valkyries square off against the Sparks
stories.summary: Golden State Valkyries (31-12, 14-8 Western Conference) at Los Angeles Sparks (16-27, 9-13 Western Conference)
stories.body:
Golden State Valkyries (31-12, 14-8 Western Conference) at Los Angeles Sparks (16-27, 9-13 Western Conference)

Los Angeles; Thursday, 10 p.m. EDT

BOTTOM LINE: Nneka Ogwumike and the Los Angeles Sparks host Veronica Burton and the Golden State Valkyries in Western Conference play Thursday.

The Sparks are 9-13 against Western Conference opponents. Los Angeles ranks third in the WNBA with 21.8 assists per game. Erica Wheeler leads the Sparks averaging 5.0.

The Valkyries are 14-8 in Western Conference play. Golden State is fifth in the Western Conference with 33.2 rebounds per game led by Kiah Stokes averaging 5.6.

Los Angeles' average of 8.7 made 3-pointers per game this season is just 0.7 more made shots on average than the 8.0 per game Golden State gives up. Golden State's 42.3% shooting percentage from the field this season is 5.1 percentage points lower than Los Angeles has allowed to its opponents (47.4%).

The teams play for the third time this season. The Valkyries won the last meeting 84-78 on Aug. 9, with Cecilia Zandalasini scoring 15 points in the victory.

TOP PERFORMERS: Ogwumike is averaging 17.3 points and 8.9 rebounds for the Sparks. Dearica Hamby is averaging 8.8 points over the last 10 games.

Burton is scoring 12.1 points per game and averaging 3.7 rebounds for the Valkyries. Gabby Williams is averaging 1.4 made 3-pointers over the last 10 games.

LAST 10 GAMES: Sparks: 4-6, averaging 82.2 points, 30.1 rebounds, 20.8 assists, 8.9 steals and 4.0 blocks per game while shooting 45.7% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 86.1 points per game.

Valkyries: 7-3, averaging 78.2 points, 35.8 rebounds, 20.7 assists, 8.0 steals and 4.3 blocks per game while shooting 40.9% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 69.2 points.

INJURIES: Sparks: Aaliyah Nye: out (ankle), Dearica Hamby: out (knee), Cameron Brink: out (ankle).

Valkyries: Gabby Williams: day to day (reconditioning), Cecilia Zandalasini: day to day (reconditioning), Iliana Rupert: out for season (pregnancy), Janelle Salaun: day to day (reconditioning).
